title: A306559 - self-describing English-words sequence identified with its morphic fixed point (Lean 4)
description: theorem A306559 (proved, kernel-pure): existence and uniqueness of the self-describing sequence of OEIS A306559 - the rule 'lengths of runs of consonants between successive vowels of the concatenated English names is the sequence itself', seed 1,2,3 over the finite lexicon {ZERO,ONE,TWO,THREE} (vowels {E,O}). Proved: the candidate aStar = [1,2,3] concatenated with the morphic word 0.W(0).W^2(0).W^3(0)... (W : 0 -> 11, 1 -> 01, defined as an MSB-to-LSB fold on the bits of n+1, its morphism equations proved as theorems) satisfies the describing equation for every index k (EX, by blockwise vowel tracking: each morphic name contributes exactly its W-image pair of runs), and every sequence sharing the seed and the equation equals aStar (UN, by strong induction on vowel positions). This machine-verifies the on-entry conjectured morphic form; Neder's equivalence with the tail of A039982 (informal OEIS note, 2019) is cited as prior work, not re-proved. Documented open, not claimed: the density-2/3 conjecture and the A039982 coincidence as properties of the entry. Trust base: standard axioms only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] audited on all 132 declarations; zero sorry, zero native_decide; 5 modules (proof, frozen spec, spec check, anti-vacuity check, axioms report).
